I was sitting in a coffee shop a few weeks ago, just working on my laptop, minding my own business, when I overheard two people at the next table talking about something.
Something about their conversation sounded oddly familiar, so I kept half listening while pretending to focus on my screen.
One of them mentioned a summer camp from years ago, a pretty specific one, in a small town I hadn't thought about in ages.
I went to that exact camp when I was eleven years old.
I mean, what are the odds of hearing someone randomly mention it in a coffee shop across the entire country?
I told myself it was probably just a coincidence, a common camp name, nothing more than that.
But then the guy said something even more specific, a story about a camp counselor falling into the lake during a canoe trip.
I remembered that exact moment clearly.
I was there.
I saw it happen with my own eyes.
At that point, I couldn't just sit there anymore pretending not to listen, so I turned around and asked, a little awkwardly, if they were talking about the camp on Miller Lake.
Both of them just stared at me for a second, completely confused about how a random stranger knew that detail.
Turns out, one of them had actually been at that same camp, the same summer as me, just in a different group entirely.
We spent the next twenty minutes going back and forth, trying to remember names, cabin numbers, random little details from over a decade ago.
We never actually met back then, as far as we could tell, but we clearly shared a whole summer of memories without ever really knowing each other existed.
It was honestly one of the strangest, most fun conversations I've had with a total stranger in years, the kind you can't really plan or expect.
The friend I was actually there to meet showed up halfway through and just stood there completely lost, wondering how I'd apparently made two new friends in the time it took her to find parking.
I tried to explain the whole camp thing, but honestly, it sounded even more unbelievable out loud than it had felt in the moment.

Before they left, we exchanged numbers, just in case we ever wanted to swap more old camp stories later on, and my friend just shook her head the whole time, still not quite believing what she'd walked into.
I still think about it sometimes, how close we probably walked past each other a hundred times that summer, and it took a random coffee shop years later for our paths to actually cross.
